## Series Overview

I run local-AI experiments on real industrial defect-inspection imagery — semiconductor,
casting X-ray, wafer maps — and post them in public, LinkedIn-first, with the full technical
detail (code, numbers, failure cases) landing here. The goal isn't a highlight reel: every post
ends with an honest limitation, not just a win.

The recurring question behind the series: **how far does a model that's never seen this kind of
imagery actually get, and what does it take to close the gap for real use?**

### Posts in this series

1. **Part 1** — MODUS (EPFL's any-to-any multimodal model) on real casting crack/void images.
   [LinkedIn post](#) — general multimodal models read a defect X-ray as a generic
   "bearing/mechanical component"; no domain fine-tuning.
2. **Part 2** — Zero-shot benchmark: Opus, Sonnet, and three small local VLMs (LFM2-VL-450M,
   Qwen2.5-VL-3B, Cosmos-Reason2-2B) classifying WM-811K wafer maps blind. [LinkedIn post](#) —
   frontier models scored 7-8/9; local VLMs scored 1-2/9, mostly by riding one default answer
   regardless of the image.
3. **Part 3** — [Fine-Tuning LFM2-VL-450M for X-ray Defect Detection and Localization](03-finetuning-lfm2-vl-xray-defects.qmd)
   LoRA fine-tuning on real GDXray casting X-ray images, targeting both *is there a
   defect* and *where is it*, with Outlines-constrained structured generation. Detection improved;
   localization never did — and I show exactly why.
4. **Part 4** — [Fine-Tuning LFM2.5-VL-3B — Does the Grounding Upgrade Actually Help?](04-finetuning-lfm25-vl-xray-defects.qmd)
   Same task, dataset, and eval split as Part 3, testing Liquid AI's newer,
   grounding-improved 3B model. Detection improved again; localization still didn't work, but
   failed in a more specific way — plausible box *size*, near-random box *position*.
5. **Part 5** — [Can a Small Local VLM Catch Its Own Auto-Labeling Mistakes?](05-lfm25-vl-label-qa-judge.qmd)
   — this post. Same model and eval split, different question: verification instead of
   generation. Few-shot examples nearly doubled the judge's recall on synthetically corrupted
   labels — while going to a flat 0% on the one error type (a real defect mislabeled clean) that
   matters most, traced back to a gap in the demo set itself.

## Tools used throughout

- Local inference on a DGX Spark (GB10, unified memory) — no cloud GPU rental
- HuggingFace `transformers` + `peft` for models and LoRA
- [Outlines](https://github.com/dottxt-ai/outlines) for schema-constrained generation
- Real, licensed datasets with ground truth (GDXray, WM-811K) — underlying ground truth is always
  real; Part 5's label-QA task deliberately corrupts *proposed* labels to simulate auto-labeling
  errors, clearly marked as synthetic where it's used

Code for every post is public. Links inline.
